setlist.title: Beat It On Down the Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (1 review, 1 other source): Extraordinarily hot Good Lovin', considered on another level from other pre-1971 versions; Listed with a drums segment leading into Good Lovin' at the end of the show [3][13]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums leading into The Other One may be the longest such stretch, running over 16 minutes [11]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One is a sweet version that eventually moves into Casey Jones; Truckin' > Drums > Other One anchors the electric set [11]
- **Attics Of My Life** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Attics as a great version [9]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): The band doesn't sing the words but plays the sustained 'gone, gone, gone' notes, showing the song's development [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Operator**: rare: 4 archived performances [14]
- **How Long Blues**: rare: 5 archived performances [14]
- **Truck Drivin' Man**: rare: 14 archived performances [14]
- **Together Again**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Sweet Lovin' One**: rare: 5 archived performances [14]
- **Sweet Lovin' One**: rare: 5 archived performances [14]
- **Dirty Business**: rare: 12 archived performances [14]
- **Connection**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd70-11-07.aud.warner.10306.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 35 songs; 211 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [1]. Said about its sound: Audio levels and quality swing dramatically between songs, as if from different tapings, forcing the listener to keep adjusting volume and EQ; Audience recording that improves when equalized for playback; reviewer calls it a masterpiece of the audience-taping style [6][8]
- **gd1970-11-07.aud.toner.berger.100330.flac16**: audience recording; 17 songs; 90 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Decent audience recording for the period; each set is incomplete and every song has cuts, with plenty of crowd chatter [9]
- **gd1970-11-07.134083.aud.weinberg.parish.flac16**: audience recording; 10 songs; 55 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording is muddy with buzzing bass, in poor quality overall [13]
- **gd1970-11-07.aud.weinberg.moore.berger.98264.flac16**: audience recording; 7 songs; 37 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Decent audience tape for its era, but with many cuts and fluctuating sound levels [7]

## Around the show

- Conversations among audience members are audible amid the music on the recording [6]
- This recording covers the third set of the late show; the crowd energy is good [7]
- Reportedly less exciting than the other November 1970 Port Chester shows, though the reviewer enjoys the acoustic set [11]
- Good Lovin' here is rated above great versions from 11/6/70 and 12/31/70 [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-11-07.aud.warner.10306.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Ken Leigh, Jack Toner and Marty Weinberg; transferred by Jack Warner; source: Audience [1]
- **gd1970-11-07.aud.toner.berger.100330.flac16**: taped by Jack Toner; transferred by Rob Berger; source: AUD > Master Cassette [2]
- **gd1970-11-07.134083.aud.weinberg.parish.flac16**: taped by Marty Weinberg; transferred by Michael Parish and Rob Berger; source: source: aud reel master; taped by Marty Weinberg; akg d190e > uher 4000L; transferred by Michael Parish; seeded by Rob Berger [3]
- **gd1970-11-07.aud.weinberg.moore.berger.98264.flac16**: taped by Marty Weinberg; transferred by Rob Berger; source: mastered on uher reel w/akg d190e mics taped by Marty Weinberg [4]
